description: MS IT researcher (University of Sargodha, Pakistan) working on multi-agent RL, RAG and federated learning. We are building EarthTrend Copilot: detect long-term trends in NASA Earth data (MODIS NDVI, land surface temperature, precipitation) for regions like Punjab, plus a RAG assistant that answers questions with charts and data citations. Looking for 1-2 members: frontend/data visualization (Streamlit/React) and Earth science or data analysis. Python preferred.
summary: EarthTrend Detective is a free web tool that turns students and the public into Earth-science data detectives. Users answer three questions (where, what and when) and the app pulls NASA data live: MERRA-2 reanalysis and GEWEX SRB/CERES radiation through NASA POWER (1981-2025), plus MODIS vegetation greenness (2000-present). It plots the long-term time series, measures the rate of change with a 95% confidence interval, and tests whether the trend is statistically significant using Mann-Kendall (corrected for autocorrelation and seasonality), a regression t-test and a Pettitt change-point test, then explains the result in plain language. A Variable Scanner finds which of 20 variables are trending at a place, with false-discovery-rate control, and a Trend Map tests every grid cell in a region to show how the same variable can rise in one place and fall next door. Examples: Svalbard is warming +0.79 C per decade (about 4x the global rate); East African rainfall rose significantly in 68 grid cells and fell in 20. Every statistical routine is validated against SciPy and pymannkendall.
details: WHAT IT DOES: EarthTrend Detective answers the four questions of the challenge: what is changing, where, how much, and is the change statistically significant? (1) Choose a variable: 20 NASA variables in six everyday themes (heat; rain and humidity; soil water and drought; plants and greenness; sunlight and clouds; wind and air), each with a plain-language definition. A place-type helper (city, farmland, desert, rainforest, polar, coast) suggests variables likely to show change. (2) Get data for a region: click anywhere on the map; data are downloaded live from NASA APIs, so nothing is pre-processed. (3) Visualize: annual mean, any season, any month, or every month with the seasonal cycle removed. Charts show observations, the Theil-Sen trend with its 95% confidence band, the least-squares line and any change point, plus a chart comparing the early and late seasonal cycle. (4) Test significance: Theil-Sen slope with 95% CI; Mann-Kendall; modified Mann-Kendall (Yue and Wang 2004) for autocorrelation; seasonal Mann-Kendall (Hirsch 1982) for monthly data; OLS t-test with 95% CI plus an autocorrelation-adjusted version (Santer 2000); Pettitt change-point test; and an estimate of how many more years are needed if a trend is not yet significant. The app warns when tests disagree and explains every verdict in plain words. BEYOND ONE PLACE: The Variable Scanner tests 19 NASA POWER variables (plus optional MODIS NDVI) at once and ranks them by Benjamini-Hochberg q-value to prevent false discoveries. The Trend Map runs the full test on every 0.5 x 0.625 degree grid cell in a region up to 10 x 10 degrees, showing that one variable can trend in opposite directions in neighbouring regions (East Africa rainfall: 68 cells significantly wetter, 20 significantly drier). Eight one-click Case Files (Arctic warming, hot nights in Punjab, greening farmland, Sahel rainfall, Amazon dry season, Aral Sea, East Africa, Lahore urban heat) and a Learn and Methods page make it classroom-ready. Results can be exported as CSV, charts saved as PNG, and investigations shared by link. IMPACT: Students, teachers, farmers and planners can run a real scientific trend analysis in under a minute without coding, downloads or accounts, and learn what statistically significant really means. TOOLS: Static web app (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) on GitHub Pages; Plotly.js charts; Leaflet maps; a dependency-free JavaScript statistics engine validated by an automated Python test suite (SciPy, NumPy, pymannkendall) on 80 synthetic series, agreeing to better than one part in a million; Playwright end-to-end tests. Source code: https://github.com/iammalik884/earthtrend-detective
